title: Rate-Limiting Time: debounceTime, throttleTime, and distinctUntilChanged

questions.prompt: Which operator waits for a quiet gap and then emits the latest value — ideal for detecting that a user stopped typing?
questions.explanation: debounceTime holds each value until dueTime passes with no new emission, then emits the latest — the classic 'done typing' detector.

questions.prompt: By default, `throttleTime(300)` emits which value of each window?
questions.explanation: throttleTime defaults to { leading: true, trailing: false }, so it emits the first value of each window and ignores the rest. Enable trailing, or use auditTime, to get the latest.

questions.prompt: Why does `distinctUntilChanged()` fail to drop `{id:1}, {id:1}` duplicates?

options.text: It compares with === by default, and two distinct object literals are never ===
It compares against all previous values, not the last one
It requires the stream to complete first

questions.explanation: The default comparator is strict equality. Different object references are not ===, so nothing is dropped. Use a comparator or distinctUntilKeyChanged('id').

questions.prompt: You need at most one scroll update per 100ms, and you want the LATEST scroll position each window. Which operator fits best?
questions.explanation: auditTime emits the most recent value at the end of each window (trailing edge). Leading-edge throttleTime would give the first (stale) position; debounceTime would wait for scrolling to stop entirely.

questions.prompt: Complete the typeahead pipeline order: `map(...) → ____________(300) → distinctUntilChanged()`. Type the operator name.
questions.explanation: The standard recipe settles input with debounceTime, then skips unchanged values with distinctUntilChanged (before flattening into a request).

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: distinct() remembers every value it has seen, which can grow memory unbounded
Put debounceTime before an expensive request, not after

questions.explanation: distinctUntilChanged is consecutive-only; distinct keeps a Set of all values; debounce belongs early in the pipe. throttle and debounce solve different problems (rate-limit vs settle) and are not interchangeable.
